svg.title: Building Closing Certainty Before the Buyer Arrives
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-closing-certainty-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Building Closing Certainty Before the Buyer Arrives; subtitle: Clean books, honest disclosure, binding exclusivity, and protected seller money; caption: Closing certainty starts with tax returns that tie to P&Ls and an honest CIM. It continues with 60-to-90-day exclusivity and a seller note carrying offset rights, all run fast enough to beat deal fatigue.; assumptions note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame, not a practitioner timeline. The reported target close is 3 to 6 months, with fatigue at 4 to 6 months.; note: Sources are Charles Weatherly, iGOTHAM, Patrick O'Connell, Quiet Light Brokerage, My SBA Loan Pro Podcast (Jake Parsley), and Amped Success (Mark Sims).; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Tie the Books; deliverable: Three years of tax returns tied to the P&L line by line, with unreceipted add-backs stripped; gate: No listing goes out until every add-back has a receipt; week: Week 2; title: Disclose and Draft the CIM; deliverable: Settled suits, state tax matters, and change-of-control leases disclosed in an honest CIM; gate: No hidden weakness that would surface at week six as broken trust; week: Week 3; title: Lock the LOI; deliverable: LOI or IOI covering price, terms, and 60 to 90 days of binding exclusivity; gate: Reject 100% seller-financed full-price LOIs unless it is a partner buyout; week: Week 4; title: Protect the Close; deliverable: Seller note with an offset right and a data-request turnaround inside the month; gate: Keep part of the seller's money in the buyer's pocket instead of escrow
